title: Duskwood
body: Duskwood was once called Brightwood, a green and peaceful stretch of the forests south of Stormwind, dotted with farms and hamlets. Then a foul magic seeped into the land, and the woods fell under a night that never fully lifts. The dead do not rest here. The necromancer Morbent Fel commands skeletons and ghouls from the graveyards of Raven Hill, and worgen have appeared as if from thin air to overrun the groves and orchards. Dark Riders out of Deadwind Pass have slaughtered a farmer's family, and the Defias Brotherhood squats in abandoned farmsteads. When Stormwind recalled its guards, the people of Darkshire raised the Night Watch to defend themselves, and they bitterly resent the capital that left them alone. At the forest's heart the Twilight Grove keeps a gateway to the Emerald Dream, the realm of the green dragonflight.

title: The Hushed Bank
body: The Hushed Bank is the quiet northwestern shore of Duskwood's river, close to the Westfall border. Here Sven Yorgen keeps a small camp with his companion Lars, far from the safety of Darkshire. They are so few that they cannot spare a man to fetch supplies, and the Carevin family sends what it can with any willing traveler. The two must hunt for their own food, and starving and rabid dire wolves come out of the trees whenever meat is carried back to camp. Venom web spiders and green recluses nest along the bank, and from this lonely post Sven plots against the necromancer to the east.

title: The Darkened Bank
body: The Darkened Bank follows the river that runs the whole length of Duskwood's northern edge. Starving and rabid dire wolves hunt along it, the rare wolf Lupos among them, while venom web spiders nest between the foothills and the water. Their legs are prized in Darkshire, where the tavern cook turns them into a tangy dish he insists on calling crab cakes. Ghouls and skeletons stray down to the banks from the cemeteries to the south. Between the wolves, the spiders and the restless dead, few travelers care to linger beside these dark waters.

title: Addle's Stead
body: Just south of the road from Westfall, where it first enters Duskwood, stands Addle's Stead, a farm abandoned to the darkness and then claimed by the Defias Brotherhood. Night runners, night blades and Defias enchanters lurk in its fields, its barn and its little farmhouse, and a Defias strongbox sits among the buildings. The Night Watch counts any Defias presence a threat, and Watcher Backus heard reports that agents of the Brotherhood had gathered here a couple of weeks ago, as though something big had taken place.

title: Raven Hill
body: Raven Hill was once a town of western Duskwood, but it has long stood abandoned, its houses empty and its streets given over to the Unseen, shadowy things that drift through the ruins. Lately something else has been seen there. Calor of Darkshire swears the buildings are haunted: two nights running he noticed shadows moving, and on the night before that a light in one of the windows. A goblin trader named Bliztik has found shelter among the deserted buildings, and the graveyard that gives the town its grim fame lies just to the north.

parts.body: The haunting of Raven Hill is no monster. The moving shadows and the light in the window belong to Jitters, a terrified fugitive who has taken refuge among the empty houses. He shrinks from every stranger, begging to be left alone, sure that whatever hunts him is everywhere and that he cannot escape it.

title: Raven Hill Cemetery
body: North of the abandoned town sprawls the Raven Hill Cemetery, which by the end of the wars had grown to dominate much of the area. It holds the graves of many who met tragic ends, and few of them lie still. Skeletal horrors walk among the headstones, ghouls such as flesh eaters, bone chewers and rotted ones claw at the earth, and plague spreaders infest the eastern mausoleum. Grave robbers pick over whatever the dead leave behind. One stone bears only the name Eliza and a prayer that the earth might satisfy her hunger, and close by, on the cemetery's edge, the old hermit Abercrombie keeps his lonely shack.

title: Forlorn Rowe
body: The Forlorn Rowe is the hill on the northern edge of the Raven Hill Cemetery, and the house at its top is the lair of the necromancer Morbent Fel. From there he looks down on the graves below and commands the dead of Duskwood. Skeletal raiders, warders and healers guard the slopes, and a skeletal officer called Commander Felstrom walks among them. Out past the house lies a weathered grave whose marker reads simply Morgan Ladimore, and the dirt over it has recently been disturbed, a good deal of it displaced.

title: The Yorgen Farmstead
body: In western Duskwood, southeast of Sven Yorgen's camp, lies the farm he once worked with his wife and children, until Dark Riders out of Deadwind Pass descended on it while he was away and slaughtered his family. Returning, Sven glimpsed a shadowy figure burying something behind an old stump near the barn, but the man fled before he could be caught. The farm was never reclaimed. Defias night runners, night blades and enchanters now lurk around the empty buildings, and young black ravagers prowl the woods around them.

parts.body: Behind the stump lies a mound of dirt, piled up in haste by someone with little time to hide what he carried. Buried in it is a small, dirt-stained book with no title, and when Sven read its pages he slammed it shut: its writer had witnessed the slaughter of his family.

parts.body: The witness was a fugitive who had hidden in Sven's barn for days without making himself known. His completed journal tells what the riders wanted. Before the killing began they demanded the Scythe of Elune of Sven's wife. She bravely claimed to know it, hoping to lead them away from her children, but a power working through a rider's gem found her lie, a voice declared that the Lord had spoken, and the family was killed.
sources: page_text 192-203 (Jitters' Completed Journal, item 2560, given on accepting quest 268)

title: Vul'Gol Ogre Mound
body: In southern Duskwood, near where the road turns south toward Stranglethorn Vale, a basin of ruined farmhouses has become the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound, home of the Splinter Fist ogres. Warriors, fire weavers and taskmasters crowd the hollow under a brute named Zzarc'Vul, who wears a monocle large enough to serve as the lens of a stargazing device. The ogres raid beyond their mound as well. When the hermit Abercrombie wandered too far from home picking herbs, a band of them chased him off and carried his crate of tools and herbs back to their lair.

title: Twilight Grove
body: At the heart of Duskwood stands the Twilight Grove, where a great tree rises above a moonwell and a gazebo of night elf design, strange sights so far from Kalimdor. The grove holds one of the few gateways to the Emerald Dream, the realm watched over by the green dragonflight. It is one of four such gateways, each beneath a great tree; the others lie at Seradane in the Hinterlands, Bough Shadow in Ashenvale and Dream Bough in Feralas.

title: The Rotting Orchard
body: Southwest of Darkshire the orchards of Duskwood have gone to rot, and the worgen have overrun them. Nightbane dark runners, which make up the bulk of the worgen packs, roam between the twisted trees alongside shadow weavers, and the Unseen drift through the gloom. Hunters of the Carevin family come here to thin their numbers. Just to the east lies the mine called Roland's Doom, where the worgen were first found, and where the fiercest of them now make their den around their bonfires.

title: Brightwood Grove
body: West of Darkshire the forest opens into Brightwood Grove, a name kept from the days when the whole wood was called Brightwood. Nothing bright remains. Nightbane worgen keep camps throughout the grove, shadow weavers and dark runners among them, and the dreaded worgen Fenros stalks between them. Black ravagers and their mastiffs hunt in packs across the fields, and green recluse spiders spin in the trees. Calor of the Carevin family, scoffing at the name, sends those who would join his master's cause here first to prove themselves against the worgen.

title: Darkshire
body: Darkshire, once called Grand Hamlet, took its grim name after darkness fell on the forest. It is the heart of human Duskwood and the home of the Night Watch. Lord Ello Ebonlocke governs from the town hall with a council that complains endlessly of Stormwind's neglect, while Commander Althea Ebonlocke leads the watchers. Clerk Daltry keeps the town registry, the Scarlet Raven Tavern serves Chef Grual's spider leg crab cakes, Madame Eva reads the cards beside the square, and the Carevin family plots its own war on evil. The stargazer Viktori seeks answers in the sky, certain that a truth beyond magic can explain the forest's strange transformation.

title: Tranquil Gardens Cemetery
body: Just south of Darkshire lies the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, whose name has become a bitter joke. Skeletal warriors and mages rise among the graves, and the Night Watch sends its first volunteers here to cut them down before they reach the town. A deranged ghoul haunts the ruined church. In the hills nearby stands the old farmhouse of Blind Mary, a spirit who tore out her own eyes and believes herself a monster, and who still begs visitors not to look at her. She once threw her prized looking glass away behind the barn, and rumor says the ghoul may have picked it up.

title: Manor Mistmantle
body: Just north of Darkshire stands Manor Mistmantle, the house of the recluse Stalvan Mistmantle. The grounds have gone to rot. Fetid corpses shamble along the overgrown paths and around the house, and the Unseen drift nearby. Only one living thing seems to thrive there, a single flower in the garden called the Tear of Tilloa. Its master is no welcoming host. He meets intruders with threats to spill their blood, and sometimes, peering at them, mistakes them for someone named Tilloa.

parts.body: The manor hides a murderer. Stalvan, once a scholar and tutor, became obsessed with Tilloa, the daughter of the noble family he served, and when she chose another his longing turned to blood. The Night Watch had kept a suspicious eye on the house for some time before proof of its master's guilt was found, and Commander Ebonlocke ordered him executed.
sources: quest 80 description (I have had my eye on that creep)

title: Beggar's Haunt
body: In the northeast of Duskwood, close to the road into Deadwind Pass, stands Beggar's Haunt, an abandoned scout tower of the Stormwind Guard. Its new tenants are Forsaken. Deathstalker Zraedus and Apothecary Faustin of the Royal Apothecary Society belong to an expeditionary force sent at Varimathras's command to survey the southern lands, and they would rather nobody knew they were here. When a human infiltrator was caught spying on the tower and carried off to the orcs of Stonard, they resolved to help their orcish allies, after their own fashion, and Faustin set about brewing a truth serum for the prisoner.

title: Commander Althea Ebonlocke
body: Commander Althea Ebonlocke leads the Night Watch, the militia Darkshire raised for itself after Stormwind withdrew its commissioned guards. She has never had enough watchers, and she warns every traveler to keep to the roads and move only by day. The defense of the town comes before everything, and she has little patience for dead end leads. She sends volunteers against the undead of the cemeteries, and against Mor'Ladim, a wandering undead who attacks her watchmen on patrol and has slain some of her strongest watchers.
sources: npc_text 50029 (stick to the roads, travel by day, numbers small)
quest 79 completion text (Darkshire's defense is my priority, no time for dead-end leads)
quest 227 reward text (attacking Watchmen on patrol)
notes: Converted: her suspicion of Stalvan and the execution order moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 98); Mor'Ladim's fall and her confession about Sarah added as part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 229, offered on the 228 turn-in). Mor'Ladim stays in the opening as she presents him (quest 227 reward text). npc_text 50029 reread: nothing from later builds. Faction 1: Althea uses faction template 53 (Night Watch), hostile to Horde.

parts.body: One man had long troubled her: Stalvan Mistmantle, the creep in the manor north of town, on whom she had kept a wary eye for some time. When a trail of letters and journal pages, matched by Clerk Daltry to the registry signature, proved his guilt, she knew her suspicions had been right, and she ordered the murderer executed once and for all.

When Mor'Ladim was finally struck down, she thanked his slayer on behalf of Darkshire and then confessed what she should have said earlier. Morgan Ladimore, whose undead body Mor'Ladim was, had believed his whole family dead, but his daughter Sarah lived, and now serves as a Watcher, always troubled by the circumstances of her father's death.

title: Lord Ello Ebonlocke
body: Lord Ello Ebonlocke is the Mayor of Darkshire, presiding over its council from the town hall. He has no illusions about his town's position. Undead crawl all over the land, he says, and the Night Watch alone cannot protect Darkshire forever; it needs the backing of the Stormwind Army, whose guards were withdrawn from the town and left it to its own devices. He passes sentence on the worst of criminals, condemning to death a man who sold corpses to Morbent Fel, though Stormwind's House of Nobles chose to keep the villain in a cell instead.
sources: quest 377 description (Lord Ebonlocke's sentence on Dextren Ward)
quest 160 completion and reward text (does not know Abercrombie, ancient language)
creature_text 263 (Where is the Stormwind Army; the Night Watch alone cannot protect us)
notes: Converted: Lakeshire's plea and his refusal removed from the opening, since that is Redridge's Letters from Lakeshire chain (redridge.json 4422 part 5, QUEST_DONE 146); the Night Watch's origin now rests on quest 56 and creature_text 263 instead of quest 146. The Abercrombie letter and the Embalmer moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 252) and the heart to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 253). Faction 1: Ello uses faction template 12 (Stormwind), hostile to Horde. Check: confirmed it no longer tells the other zone's chain.

parts.body: A note came to him from a hermit named Abercrombie, a man he had never heard of, written in a script too ancient to read. Translated by the historian Sirra Von'Indi, it was a gloating confession from one who signed himself the Embalmer and had tricked his helpers into building a fiend of flesh, bone and twisted metal. Ello went white, and told the bearer that their kindness had doomed the town.

The Embalmer, Ello knew, was a name from Darkshire's children's stories, and he sent for the heart the hermit had placed in his dead wife Eliza. When it came back from her grave still beating, he declared it proof against the Embalmer's evil and a powerful aegis over Darkshire, and promised the deed a place in the town's annals forever.

title: Madame Eva
body: Madame Eva reads the cards and listens to the whispers of spirits from her home on the Darkshire square. The stars, she says, speak of horrors waiting in the night. When a disturbance rippled through her veins she knew her granddaughter Alyssa was in danger, and Death stared up at her from the table. A long trance gave her one name, Stalvan, and she fears for them all. She practices other old arts too, spinning thread from ghost hair that can bind spirits, and enchanting totems that punish anyone who raises a hand against their bearer.
sources: quest 148 description (her home on the Darkshire square)
quests 149, 157 (Ghost Hair Thread binds evil spirits)
notes: Converted: 'the hunt that unmasked a murderer' moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 98, turned in to Eva). Faction 1: Madame Eva uses faction template 12 (Stormwind).

parts.body: Her premonition proved true. The trail it began led to Stalvan Mistmantle, a murderer living just north of Darkshire, and when he was slain she knew it before his family ring was laid before her: a wave of hope had rippled through the tainted forest. Duskwood was free of his bloodthirst at last, though her joy was hampered by thoughts of those who fell prey to him.

title: Sven Yorgen
body: Sven Yorgen farmed land in western Duskwood until the day he went to Darkshire and came home to find his wife and children murdered by Dark Riders from Deadwind Pass. He rode after the killers, and so never learned what the shadowy figure he glimpsed by his barn had buried. Now he keeps a small camp on the Hushed Bank with his companion Lars, living off the land, short of men and welcoming anyone who will join his fight. Dangerous days lie ahead, Lars says, with the necromancer to the east.
sources: page_text 193 (Sven left his farm for Darkshire)
quest 55 description (be the instrument of my revenge)
notes: Converted: the riders seen with Fel and his vow of revenge moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 268); Fel's defeat added as part 2 (QUEST_DONE 55, turned in to Sven). Faction 1: Sven uses faction template 12 (Stormwind). His Cataclysm worgen transformation is deliberately absent. Check: part 1 trigger moved from QUEST_DONE 268 to QUEST_ACCEPT 323: the test against Fel's minions is quest 323's text, offered by Sven on the 268 turn-in.

parts.body: The buried book led at last to its author, and his completed journal set Sven on the path against the riders. He had seen them in Duskwood, speaking with the necromancer Morbent Fel at the Forlorn Rowe, and Fel's death became his revenge, though he would send no one against so vile a fiend without first testing their skill against his minions.

Morbent Fel was defeated. The Dark Riders are still at large, Sven admits, but a small piece of what he had hoped beyond hope has come to pass, and he promised that the deed would live forever in the legends of Duskwood. Perhaps, he said, fate would one day bring his avenger back to him.

title: Jitters
body: Jitters is a nervous, starving fugitive who hides in the empty town of Raven Hill. He has lived there for weeks on grubs and weeds, and he would trade well for a decent meal; he has heard that Chef Grual's crab cakes in Darkshire are very good. Strangers terrify him. Found, he begs not to be killed and swears there are no monsters in Raven Hill, only harmless Jitters, yet he insists that they are everywhere and that he cannot escape them.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Jitters (a member of the Defias Brotherhood infiltrating Duskwood)
notes: Converted: the opening is now the frightened man one meets (quests 163, 5). His authorship of the buried book moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 453); the journal's confession (Roland's Doom, the scythe, the worgen, the barn) moved to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 268, which hands it over). Defias link from page_text 186 and the wiki. Faction 1: Jitters uses faction template 12.

parts.body: Jitters is the shadowy figure Sven Yorgen glimpsed by his barn on the night his family died. Cornered at last, he owned that the half finished book buried behind the stump was his, and warned that whoever had read it knew only half the tale.
sources: quest 268 description (left it at Sven's farm when I fled)

parts.body: His completed journal tells the rest. Digging in the mine called Roland's Doom, with the Defias Brotherhood pleased with the work, he pulled a rune-carved scythe from the rubble, and worgen fell on the miners from every side. He believes he alone escaped, saved perhaps by the caution that gave him his nickname. Hiding in Sven's barn, he watched riders hunting that very scythe kill the family, and has fled from hiding place to hiding place since. Rather than face Sven, he gave the journal up.

title: Jonathan Carevin
body: Jonathan Carevin heads the Carevin family of Darkshire, hunters of demons, undead and other monstrosities who wage their own war against evil in the forest. He is a busy and suspicious man who trusts no one unwilling to aid the cause, and he watches the townsfolk for any who give comfort to the enemies of the Light. Among his followers is Calor, who joined the family in disgust at the complacency of the Night Watch. Calor tests recruits against the worgen and recommends the worthy to his master.
sources: quest 1042 description (Carevin family, hunters of demons, undead and monstrosities; Jonathan head of the household)
quest 223 reward text (cold reception, trust none)
quest 173 description (Calor disillusioned by the Watch)
quest 1043 reward text (influence not large enough, contain the worgen)
notes: Converted: the Carevins' resolve to contain the worgen moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 1044, offered by Jonathan on the 1043 turn-in, whose description adds that he bears Velinde no ill will). 1044 is sorted under Ashenvale but no other file uses it; it ends with Thyn'tel in Darnassus, whose side darnassus.json tells by TALK. Faction 1: Jonathan and Calor use faction template 12. Check: part 1 reworded to follow the quests' order: the tale he judged true is the one told on 1042 (1043 description), before the mine.

parts.body: He judged true the stranger's tale of a night elf priestess, and pointed to the mine to the south, where the worgen were first found. Hearing what lay there, he admits that the Carevins lack the influence to find the root of these troubles and end them once and for all, but they will contain the worgen's numbers in Duskwood, and he has made it Calor's first priority. For the priestess who brought this evil into the woods, he bears no ill will.

title: Abercrombie
body: Abercrombie is a frail old man who lives alone in a shack beside the Raven Hill Cemetery. He once came to Darkshire often for supplies, but has not been seen there in a long while; the roads are dangerous, he says, and he is not getting any younger. He seems harmless enough, asking travelers for ghost hair thread to string across his door and windows, strong liquor for the cold nights, ghoul ribs for an effigy against the ghouls, and a crate of tools stolen by ogres. Yet he laughs a little too hard when they succeed, and more than once his tongue slips, as if about to thank some darker power.
sources: quest 253 description (the Embalmer, Eliza, his heart)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Abercrombie (necromancer, the Hermit and the Embalmer, pre-Cataclysm location)
notes: Converted: his identity as the Embalmer moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 252, the translated note); the children's tale of Eliza and the heart to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 253); the heart taken and his power broken to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 253). The opening keeps his requests and the hints in his speech (quests 134, 159 reward texts). Faction 1: Abercrombie uses faction template 12, and quest 165 is Alliance only.

parts.body: His note to Lord Ebonlocke, once translated, gave him away. It was a gloating confession signed the Embalmer. The hermit called himself a creator, and he had fooled his helpers into aiding his latest and most dire creation, a fiend of flesh, bone and twisted metal now waiting outside his dwelling for his word to go forth and slaughter.

The Embalmer is a name from Darkshire's children's stories, and the story is true. He was once a kindly alchemist, driven mad by the death of his wife Eliza. To restore her he used dark magic to place his own heart within her body. It revived her, but cursed her with a hunger for human flesh, and he had to keep her buried. His heart is his power.

That heart was dug out of Eliza's grave, still beating, and carried to Lord Ebonlocke. With it the Embalmer's power was broken, and its magic became a powerful aegis over the town he had meant to see slaughtered.

title: Stalvan Mistmantle
body: Stalvan Mistmantle of Silverpine was once a scholar, an apprentice of Headmaster Crillian, who travelled south and stayed in Moonbrook to tutor the farm children, until troubles in the region forced him to abandon his post as headmaster of its new schoolhouse. Now he lives as a recluse in a rotting manor just north of Darkshire, where a single flower called the Tear of Tilloa grows in the garden. He greets intruders with threats to spill their blood, and sometimes, peering at them, takes them for someone named Tilloa.
sources: page_text 16-19 (letters to Crillian, Moonbrook Schoolhouse, Stalvan Mistmantle of Silverpine)
page_text 20-24 (Tilloa, begonia, suitor, nice old man, blood I shall spill)
notes: Converted: the opening is what one meeting him learns (creature_text 315) plus his Moonbrook past, which westfall.json 4010 and elwynn.json 1205 already tell openly. The Flintridge tutoring and his love for Tilloa moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 75, by which the torn and faded pages are read); the suitor, the vow of blood, the massacre and the proof to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 80, Daltry's match); his death added as part 3 (KILL 315 or QUEST_DONE 98), trimmed to what the kill alone tells. Faction 0: Stalvan (faction 14) can be killed by either side. Left out his brother Tobias and his Cataclysm return. Check: part 2 reworded so the Flintridge massacre (quest 72) and the slaughter of visiting nobles (quest 79) are told as each source tells them, without saying whether they were one crime or two; the proof is tied to the nobles' slaughter, where the muddy pages were found.

parts.body: Leaving Moonbrook, Stalvan became tutor to the children of the noble Flintridge family, and his journal shows what followed. The boy Giles was rambunctious, but the elder daughter, Tilloa, was exceptionally bright, and he could not help noticing her beauty, though her father had arranged her marriage for the coming year. When she placed a scarlet begonia in his palm and smiled, his heart trembled, and he took it for love.

The later pages turn dark. Sure that she shared his feelings, he was enraged when Tilloa introduced him to her suitor as her tutor, a nice old man, and when she was engaged his despair became a vow of blood. The Flintridge estate had once seen a massacre, and Tavernkeep Smitts had found the muddy pages while investigating the slaughter of visiting nobles, a crime never tied to the crazy man in the woods until Clerk Daltry matched the journal's hand to Stalvan's registry signature, proving his guilt beyond doubt.
sources: page_text 22-24 (Muddy Journal Pages 938, Bloodstained Journal Page 939)
quest 72 description (massacre at the Flintridge estate)

parts.body: Stalvan Mistmantle is dead, cut down in his own manor north of Darkshire. The scholar who once taught farm children in Moonbrook will threaten no one again, and the recluse who mistook strangers for Tilloa is silent at last.

title: Morbent Fel
body: Morbent Fel is the necromancer behind the undead plague of Duskwood. From his house atop the Forlorn Rowe he looks down on the Raven Hill Cemetery, and the skeletons and ghouls that fill it answer to his will, while skeletal raiders, warders and healers guard the slopes below him. He has human accomplices too: Dextren Ward was caught selling him bodies from the cemetery and condemned to death for it by Lord Ebonlocke. At their lonely camp on the Hushed Bank, Sven Yorgen and his companion Lars count the necromancer their enemy.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Morbent_Fel (pre-Cataclysm: ruled the undead of Duskwood, magical barrier, Morbent's Bane)
quest 323 description (ally to the dark riders)
quest 226 description and reward text (Lars and Sven against the necromancer)
notes: Converted: his alliance with the Dark Riders moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 268); his protective enchantments to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 269, Farthing's reward text; QUEST_ACCEPT 270 is wetlands.json's trigger, so the Lightforge iron is told in story 1029 part 4 instead); his defeat added as part 3 (KILL 1200 or QUEST_DONE 55), trimmed to what the kill alone tells. Faction 0: Morbent Fel (faction 21) can be killed by either side. His Cataclysm return as a lich is deliberately absent. Check: part 1 trimmed to the 268 reward text: 'ally' (quest 323) and the vow of revenge (quest 55) dropped from it; Sven's entry 1019 and story 1029 tell the vow on QUEST_ACCEPT 323.

parts.body: Fel keeps company with the Dark Riders of Deadwind Pass. Sven Yorgen has seen the riders who slaughtered his family speaking with the necromancer at the Forlorn Rowe, and the journal that told him why they killed has set him on the path against them.

Bishop Farthing of Stormwind, reading of the evil taint that has taken hold in Duskwood, judged the necromancer immensely powerful. Fel has cast dark enchantments about himself to protect him from physical assaults, and whoever means to defeat him must first carry a weapon that is proof against those protections.
Morbent Fel has fallen, slain in his house above the Raven Hill Cemetery, and the master of Duskwood's restless dead no longer looks down on the graves from the Forlorn Rowe.

title: Mor'Ladim
body: Mor'Ladim is the name taken by an undead knight who wanders Duskwood, following a strange and meandering path through the Raven Hill Cemetery and the woods around it. He kills without reason, attacking watchmen on patrol and travelers alike, and some of the Night Watch's strongest watchers have been lost to him. Darkshire wants him laid to rest, but Commander Ebonlocke has no one to spare for the task and can only wish luck to those who try.
sources: quest 227 reward text (attacking watchmen on patrol and killing people)
notes: Converted: the opening is the undead one meets and what Althea says of him (quests 227 reward, 228). Who he was moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 227, the book, or QUEST_ACCEPT 228, which follows it); his fall added as part 2 (KILL 522 or QUEST_DONE 228); Sarah's survival and his rest moved to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 231). Check part 2's second sentence: a Horde killer never reaches 231, but the line only says rest is still to come, which the Alliance chain bears out (228 reward text, one small matter). Faction 0: Mor'Ladim (faction 21) can be killed by either side, though quest 228 is only reachable through Alliance NPCs. Check: part 1 trigger QUEST_ACCEPT 227 replaced by QUEST_DONE 227 (the book is 227's reward item; QUEST_ACCEPT 228 kept, it follows). Part 2 no longer names Morgan Ladimore or says his rest is still to come: a Horde character earns it by KILL 522 alone, which reveals neither.

parts.body: He was once Morgan Ladimore, a noble knight of Duskwood who fought beside Uther the Lightbringer in the wars of Lordaeron. He came home to find his house in ruins and his wife Lys beneath a gravestone at Raven Hill. Mad with grief, he cut down three cemetery attendants who tried to restrain him, then turned his knife on himself. Buried without ceremony, he rose only days later.
sources: page_text 64-72 (The Story of Morgan Ladimore, given on accepting quest 227)

parts.body: Mor'Ladim has been struck down among the graves he haunts. The undead knight who cut down watchmen and travelers without reason lies still at last, and the patrols of the Night Watch have one less terror to face on the roads around Raven Hill.
sources: quest 228 reward text (there is one small matter)

parts.body: Morgan never knew that one of his children had lived. His daughter Sarah now serves as a Watcher, and she sent her ring to his grave so that he might know she was well and that none of them held him to blame. His spirit found peace at last, gave up his sword Archeus to the one who brought him word, and spoke his wife's name as it was put to rest.

title: The Night Watch
body: When Stormwind recalled its commissioned guards, Darkshire formed the Night Watch from its own people, and Commander Althea Ebonlocke has never had enough of them. She sends volunteers first against the skeletons of the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, then against the walking dead of Raven Hill, and finally into the eastern mausoleum to purge the plague spreaders. Watchers at a camp out on the road fight spiders that have strung up their comrades in webs. The town's anger at Stormwind runs deep. When the House of Nobles imprisoned the corpse seller Dextren Ward rather than behead him as Lord Ebonlocke had sentenced, Councilman Millstipe offered a reward for the villain's hand, a message to the nobles that Duskwood would not be ignored.
sources: quest 245 description and completion text; DB: Watcher Dodds 888 at the road camp at -10923,-385
notes: Converted: Lakeshire's plea, Ebonlocke's refusal and Solomon's suspicion of treachery removed from the opening, since Redridge's Letters from Lakeshire (redridge.json 4422, QUEST_DONE 146) stages them. Althea's thanks for the cemetery purge added as part 1 (QUEST_DONE 58); Ward's death and Millstipe's warning added as part 2 (QUEST_DONE 377). Entry triggers unchanged (56, 245, 377, all Alliance only). Check: confirmed it no longer tells the other zone's chain.

parts.body: The cemeteries were scoured and the plague spreaders cut down in the eastern mausoleum. On behalf of the people of Darkshire, Althea thanked the volunteers for their bravery and dedication, for her watchers alone are still too few to keep the town safe.

Dextren Ward paid for his crimes at last, slain in the Stormwind Stockade and his hand carried back to Darkshire. Millstipe was delighted: the families of the dead had their peace, and the corrupt bureaucrats of the House of Nobles had their message. Stormwind, he warned, must rise to the needs of Duskwood's people, or Duskwood will break free from its tyranny.

title: The Legend of Stalvan
body: It begins with Madame Eva's dread. A horrible disturbance rippled through her veins one night, and she knew her granddaughter Alyssa was in great danger; Death stared up at her from the cards. A long, dark trance gave her one clue, the name Stalvan, and she sends whoever will help to the clerk in the town hall. Clerk Daltry's registry holds a record of one Stalvan Mistmantle, last recorded at the Moonbrook Schoolhouse in Westfall, an address so outdated that he would be glad of any news to keep his records clean.
notes: Converted: the opening is Eva's premonition and Daltry's first record (66, 67). Parts follow the chain: 1 the Moonbrook letter and the Goldshire lead (QUEST_ACCEPT 69), 2 Farley's messenger and the Flintridge caretaker (QUEST_ACCEPT 72), 3 the journal pages and Smitts' investigation (QUEST_ACCEPT 79, when Smitts hands over his pages), 4 the handwriting match and the execution order (QUEST_ACCEPT 98), 5 Stalvan's death and Eva's relief (QUEST_DONE 98). Kept consistent with elwynn.json, which tells only his lodging at the Lion's Pride Inn (1205) and Haggard's chest holding a journal page (1224) as setup; none of these triggers is used there. Faction 1: all quests Alliance only.

parts.body: In an old footlocker at the Moonbrook Schoolhouse lay an unsent letter from Stalvan to his old master, Headmaster Crillian, full of happy days tutoring the farm children while the town mayor built him a school. Looking again, Daltry found a second address beneath the first, half scratched out: the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire.

Innkeeper Farley remembered a messenger who fled screaming into a stormy night years before, leaving his letters behind. One, from Stalvan, was bound for the Canal District of Stormwind, where Caretaker Folsom of the Flintridge estate took it ill. His father had mopped up the blood after the massacre there, and now the family's last possessions are headed for auction.

Journal pages turned up in the Flintridge crate, in a chest at old Marshal Haggard's house, and in the keeping of Tavernkeep Smitts in Darkshire, who had followed the legend of Stalvan for years. They told of a tutor's obsession with the Flintridges' daughter Tilloa, and of his fury when she chose another. Smitts and Haggard had investigated when visiting nobles were slaughtered, but never linked the handwriting to the crazy man in the woods.

Commander Ebonlocke had long kept an eye on Stalvan, and Daltry, expert in handwriting after his years with the registry, matched the pages to the registry signature. Her suspicions were proved. The recluse of the manor north of town had led a life of depravity, innocent victims had died by his hand, and she ordered him executed once and for all.

Stalvan Mistmantle was slain in his manor, and his family ring went to Madame Eva, whose premonition had begun the hunt. She already knew. A wave of hope had rippled through the tainted forest, and Duskwood was free of his bloodthirst, though her joy was hampered by thoughts of those who fell prey to him.

title: Worgen in the Woods
body: Worgen have come to Duskwood, overrunning Brightwood Grove and the Rotting Orchard, and no one in Darkshire can say why. Calor of the Carevin family tests would-be recruits against them: first the shadow weavers of the grove and the orchard, then the dark runners who make up the bulk of the packs, and at last the vile fangs and tainted ones who den near the caves and in the mine to the south, whose bonfires can be seen from far away. The worthy earn his recommendation to Jonathan Carevin. Those who come to town asking about the wolf-men are sent to Jonathan too, for the Carevins hunt demons, undead and every other monstrosity.
sources: creature_text 3946 (Velinde Starsong: scythe granted to fight the demons of Felwood; worgen run rampant, scythe lost)
page_text 185-190 (Jitters found the scythe in Roland's Doom, worgen came)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Roland's_Doom and Scythe_of_Elune (Velinde died at Roland's Doom)
gameobject 19030 Mound of Dirt at Roland's Doom, event_script 664 summons Velinde Starsong's spirit (3946) there
notes: Converted: the opening is Calor's hunt (173, 221, 222) plus the Darkshire clerk's referral that starts 1042. The refilling packs moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 221); Roland's Doom as the root, Velinde's death and the lost Scythe to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 1043, after the spirit appears at the mound); Jitters' discovery to part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT 268, the journal). Kept consistent with ashenvale.json 33138 (her trail ends bound for Darkshire), darnassus.json 165713 and redridge.json 4418/4424 (Morganth seeks the Scythe and may have found it): the Scythe is only called lost here, with no claim about who holds it. 1042 and 1043 are sorted under Ashenvale but used by no other file. Left out Arugal, Varkas, the Wolf Cult and the Dark Riders comic. Faction 1.

parts.body: The packs do not thin. The worgen seemed to appear out of thin air, and every time the hunters make progress, more spring up to refill their ranks. Calor cannot say what evil power draws them to this unhappy realm, and puts his faith in Master Carevin to get to the bottom of it.

Jonathan pointed to the mine to the south, Roland's Doom, where the worgen were first found. There a mound of earth gave up the spirit of Velinde Starsong, a night elf priestess who had prayed for power against the demons of Felwood and been granted a scythe by Elune. She died there, lamenting her failure: the worgen run rampant, the Scythe of her goddess is lost, and she cannot say whose hand now directs its power. The Carevins mean to contain the evil she unleashed.
sources: gameobject 19030 Mound of Dirt at Roland's Doom, event_script 664 summons Velinde's spirit

parts.body: The mine holds another tale. A digger named Jitters, working Roland's Doom for the Defias Brotherhood, pulled the haft of a rune-carved scythe from a pile of rubble, and a change rippled through the tunnels. Then the worgen came, clawing from hidden holes and dropping from above, and half the men fell in the first minutes. Jitters fled, losing the scythe in his flight, and fears it was he who brought the worgen upon Duskwood.

title: Sven's Revenge
body: Sven Yorgen has one thing to ask of those who would help him. While he was away in Darkshire, Dark Riders from Deadwind Pass descended on his farm in western Duskwood and slaughtered his family. When he returned he saw a shadowy figure skulking near the barn, burying something, but the man fled, and Sven, hot on the heels of the riders, could not stay to look. Whatever was hidden lies behind the old stump near his barn, and he would be grateful to anyone who finds it.
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of quest 95. Parts follow the chain: 1 the witness's book (QUEST_DONE 230), 2 the search through Darkshire to Jitters (QUEST_DONE 453), 3 the journal and Fel (QUEST_DONE 268), 4 the Lightforge iron and Morbent's Bane (QUEST_DONE 325, turned in to Sven), 5 Fel's defeat (QUEST_DONE 55). Faction 1: the chain starts at Alliance-only 95. Check: part 3 trigger moved from QUEST_DONE 268 to QUEST_ACCEPT 323, since its last line (the test of skill) is quest 323's text.

parts.body: The mound held a small, dirt-stained book. Sven read its pages and slammed it shut: the shadowy figure had been a witness to his family's death. He has questions to ask that man, if only he knew who he was, and he hopes someone in Darkshire can link the book with its owner.

Madame Eva sensed that the book's owner was a stranger to Darkshire, though the book itself was bought there. Clerk Daltry remembered selling it a month before to a nervous, jittery man always looking over his shoulder, and Tavernkeep Smitts recalled him writing at the bar each night before fleeing west, muttering of being hunted. In the empty town of Raven Hill, Jitters admitted the book was his.

Rather than face Sven, Jitters gave up his completed journal. It told of the Scythe of Elune and the riders who killed for it, and it set Sven on the path against them, for he had seen those riders with the necromancer Morbent Fel at the Forlorn Rowe. Fel's death would be his revenge, though first he would test the skill of anyone he sent against so vile a fiend.

Fel would not fall to ordinary blows. Bishop Farthing warned that the necromancer had cast dark enchantments about himself, and sent the would-be avenger to Menethil Harbor, where Lightforge iron lay in the wreck of the Flying Osprey, lost with the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras. Murlocs had stolen most of the ingots, but they were won back, and the dwarven smith Grimand Elmore in Stormwind forged them into Morbent's Bane.

Morbent's Bane broke the necromancer's protections, and Morbent Fel was defeated in his lair above the cemetery. The Dark Riders are still at large, but Sven, who had hoped beyond hope, saw a small piece of his revenge come to pass, and promised that the deed would live forever in the legends of Duskwood.

title: Bride of the Embalmer
body: The Carevins worry about an old man who used to come into town often for supplies but has not been seen in a long while, and those sent to check on him find Abercrombie in his shack overlooking the Raven Hill Cemetery, glad of help. The roads are dangerous, he says, and he is not getting any younger. He wants ghost hair thread, which Madame Eva spins from a comb run through Blind Mary's hair; Zombie Juice from the Scarlet Raven, brewed from rot blossoms grown in skeletons' skulls; ghoul ribs for an effigy; and a crate of tools the ogres stole. Then he sends a cheerful note to his old friend, the mayor.
sources: creature_text 468 (Town Crier during the Stitches event)
smart_scripts 263 and 412 (finishing quest 252 starts the Stitches march)
notes: Converted: the opening is the hermit's requests (165 through 160). The translated confession moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 252); the Stitches march to part 2 (KILL 412; the march begins on the 252 turn-in and ends with Stitches slain); the Embalmer's tale to part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT 253); the heart to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 253). Entry point is 165 because quest 148 requires it in quest_template_addon. Faction 1.

parts.body: Lord Ebonlocke did not know him, and the note was written in an ancient script. Translated by the historian Sirra Von'Indi, it was a gloating confession: the Embalmer had tricked his helpers into building a fiend of flesh, bone and twisted metal, which waited outside his dwelling for the word to slaughter. As Sirra finished, the air grew heavy over the land, and Ello told the bearer that their kindness had doomed the town.

The abomination Stitches marched on Darkshire along the road, roaring its hunger for the town. It overran the Night Watch camp on the way, and the town crier called the defenders to gather in the center of town, where together they stood against the undead monster until the beast was slain.
sources: creature_text 468 (Town Crier during the Stitches event)
smart_scripts 263 and 412 (finishing quest 252 starts the Stitches march)

parts.body: The Embalmer, Ello explained, is a name from one of Darkshire's children's stories: a kindly alchemist driven mad by the death of his wife Eliza, who used dark magic to place his own heart within her body. It revived her but cursed her with a hunger for human flesh, and he had to keep her buried. His heart is his power, and Ello wanted it out of her grave.

In the grave lay the remains of a coffin, and within it clawed fingers scraped and rotted teeth gnashed. The Embalmer's heart was carried out still beating, and its magic became proof against his evil and a powerful aegis over Darkshire. Ello promised the deed a place in the town's annals forever.

title: A Daughter's Love
body: On the outskirts of the Raven Hill Cemetery, out past the necromancer's house on the Forlorn Rowe, stands a lonely grave apart from the rest. Its weathered marker reads simply Morgan Ladimore, with no epitaph and no prayer. The dirt over the grave has been recently disturbed, and a good deal of it seems to have been displaced. Whoever Morgan Ladimore was, Darkshire laid him to rest far from its tended graves. The town's historian, Sirra Von'Indi, may remember the name.
notes: Converted: the opening is the grave as quest 225 presents it. Parts follow the chain: 1 Sirra's book (QUEST_ACCEPT 227, which hands it over), 2 Althea's account of Mor'Ladim (QUEST_DONE 227), 3 Mor'Ladim's fall and Sarah (QUEST_ACCEPT 229, offered on the 228 turn-in), 4 the ring and Morgan's rest (QUEST_DONE 231). parts.body: Sirra Von'Indi knew Morgan well before he left for the war, a noble and good man who suffered a bad end. Sirra keeps a leatherbound book that tells his tale better than any memory can, and says that Commander Ebonlocke is the one who has handled the trouble with him of late.

The book tells of a knight who fought beside Uther the Lightbringer in Lordaeron and came home to a corrupted forest and his family's graves at Raven Hill. In his grief he killed three innocent attendants, then took his own life. Buried without ceremony, he could not rest, and days later his body was gone from the grave.

Commander Ebonlocke knows the rest. The undead thing calling itself Mor'Ladim that wanders the cemetery is Morgan's body, attacking her watchmen on patrol and killing people, and she wants him laid to rest. Her scouts say he follows a strange and meandering path through the graves.

When Mor'Ladim fell, Althea admitted what she should have said earlier. Morgan had believed all his family dead, but his daughter Sarah Ladimore had lived, and now serves as a Watcher, always troubled by the circumstances of her father's death.

Sarah slid a ring from her hand and asked that it be laid on her father's grave, so that he might know she was well and that none of them held him responsible. At the grave a ghostly voice sounded on the wind. Morgan's spirit, the weight lifted from it, gave his sword Archeus, forged to do good, to the one who brought word, and spoke his wife's name as his soul was put to rest.
